A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 33 readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on CES, OpinionQA, and Twin-2K, including predictive accuracy, calibration, ablations, and robustness analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same LLM training objective, information-gain query selection, GNN-based respondent selection, and imputation loop. The revised idealized greedy formulations concern theoretical justification rather than a documented change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CES 2024, OpinionQA, and Twin-2K coverage and geographic evaluation scenarios. Dataset descriptions, selected questions, and respondent counts are unchanged; the revised CES access link does not establish different data usage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged: Meta-Random, Meta-Greedy, and Meta-Greedy-Imp, together with the same respondent-selection and imputation variants and greedy versus multi-step planning comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 changes the stated LoRA dropout rate from 0.1 to 0.01. Other experimental settings are retained. This is a reported training-setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The query-selection, imputation, and respondent-selection ablations, sensitivity-tier analysis, multi-step planning comparison, and model-size and geographic robustness evaluations are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-trial general evaluation protocol, five-trial averages in Table 1, sensitivity averaging across seeds, and fixed-seed training information. No uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Figures 3–9 and Tables 1–2 retain their empirical results and trends. For example, Table 1 reports global accuracy of 0.488 for greedy and 0.485 for multi-step planning at the 10% budget in both versions. The dropout revision is not accompanied by revised scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces v1's asserted universal C(k)=1−1/e bound with an explicit query-budget alignment assumption involving eta and a revised two-stage guarantee of 2/(1−exp(−2 eta)). It also formalizes feasible distinct-query sequences and revises the proofs. Appendix A.2 explicitly restricts its treatment to real-valued variables, adds density and continuous-CDF conditions, and revises the martingale formulation and consistency statement. These substantially change the assumptions and scope of the theoretical justification.

C1.justification: The method and empirical contribution claims in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion remain unchanged. However, the central near-optimality claim is narrowed through Section 4 and Appendix A: the guarantee now explicitly requires query-budget alignment in addition to monotonicity and submodularity.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an interpretation of alignment as excluding problematic concentration of information in small respondent subsets. Appendix A.2 qualifies latent-entity recovery as recovery only up to the induced predictive distribution. These add substantive applicability and identifiability qualifications; experimental interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 revises LoRA dropout from 0.1 to 0.01. Appendix B.1 changes the CES access DOI from 10.7910/DVN/X11EP6 to 10.7910/DVN/CETPVT. Other implementation details, hardware information, and the code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes Nemhauser, Wolsey, and Fisher (1978), previously cited to justify Lemma A.5, from both the proof and bibliography. The related-work section and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting in Section 4 and Appendix A reorganizes theoretical explanations, introduces a copula-computation subheading, and revises notation and cross-references. v2 also adds an ICML 2026 publication note. The overall narrative and section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: The first-page layout, theorem displays, bibliography, and early appendix pages undergo limited reflow and formatting changes. All nine figures and both tables retain their content and presentation; none are added, removed, or redrawn.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the theoretical scope more defensible by replacing v1's unsupported universal C(k)=1−1/e step with an explicit alignment condition and corresponding guarantee, and by qualifying latent recovery at the distribution level. These improve precision while narrowing applicability. The empirical evidence is unchanged, alignment is not validated for the implemented selector, and notation slips remain in the revised proof of Theorem A.3, limiting the overall gain.
